keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no Muang Sua row: its Sukhothai Kingdom shapes hold the Lao uplands to 1362 and its Lan Xang row starts 1363). The page names the town and gives no dated extent, only Lan Xang's later reach 'from the border of China to Sambor'; Louangphrabang province is the reading. Infobox area: not given.

region.text: Muang Sua (Luang Prabang) and its valley on the Mekong and Nam Khan; the page gives no frontier

ledger.note: 698: Khun Lo seizes Muang Sua. Khun Lo 'seized his opportunity when the king of Nanzhao was engaged elsewhere' and took the town his father Khun Borom had awarded him; the page says Muang Sua 'was the name of Luang Phrabang following its conquest in 698'. A chronicle date (the infobox credits Khun Borom).

region.text: Muang Sua (Luang Prabang) and its valley on the Mekong and Nam Khan; the page gives no frontier

ledger.note: 709: Nanzhao occupies Muang Sua. Nanzhao 'intervened frequently in the affairs of the principalities of the middle Mekong Valley', which led in 709 to 'the occupation of Muang Sua in 709' (infobox 'Nanzhao vassal: 709-800s').

region.text: Muang Sua (Luang Prabang) and its valley on the Mekong and Nam Khan; the page gives no frontier

ledger.note: c. 800: Nanzhao's hold ends. The infobox reads 'Nanzhao vassal: 709-800s' and the page says the occupation 'probably ended well before the northward expansion of the Khmer Empire under Indravarman I (reigned 877-889)'; 800 is the infobox's start of its range, not a date the page gives.
1128: Muang Sua becomes the Sri Sattanak Kingdom (infobox 'Became Sri Sattanak Kingdom: 1128-1353'); Khun Chueang reigns 1128-1169.

region.text: Muang Sua (Luang Prabang) and its valley on the Mekong and Nam Khan; the page gives no frontier

ledger.note: 1353: Fa Ngum takes Muang Sua and founds Lan Xang. Infobox 'Lan Xang founded: 1353'; the text has him crowned at Vientiane in June 1354. Fa Ngum 'set out from Angkor at the head of a 10,000-man army' in 1349.

wars.name: Lao-Mongol invasion of Dai Viet (1297-1301)
wars.outcome: 'From 1297 to 1301, Lao troops under Mongol command invaded Dai Viet but were repulsed by the Vietnamese'; no change of border.
wars.note: Muang Sua is listed as a second Mongol dependency 1297-1300s.

certainty.note: Chronicle history with Khmer, Nanzhao, Mongol and Sukhothai overlordships; no frontier is given.

notes: State Cliopatria lacks; named by se-01-d and se-01-f (Sukhothai's c. 1299 loss, Lan Xang's 1353 founding). One page opened (a state with 3 events; budget 2-5). Not settled: (1) the early centuries are chronicle history (Khun Borom's 698 conquest is credited to Khun Lo in the text, 698-780); (2) the vassalages in the infobox (Nanzhao 709-800s, Khmer 1070-1128 and 1185-1191, Mongol 1250s-1271 and 1297-1300s, Sukhothai 1286-1297; the infobox also says Sukhothai vassal 'in 1293') belong to the suzerains' dossiers: khmer-empire, nanzhao (no dossier yet), sukhothai-kingdom (which carries 1294-1298 for 'Phrae and Muang Sua'), and the Mongol Yuan; (3) the page gives no 1298/1299 independence date, so the sukhothai-kingdom loss of c. 1299 has no support here beyond the 1297 Mongol dependency; (4) the page dates Lan Xang to 1353 in the infobox and June 1354 in the text; (5) Vieng Chan Vieng Kham (Vientiane), the other mandala between 1299 and 1357, has no dossier; (6) the occupation_end of c. 800 is confidence 1.
